analysis.session_summary: The full trading day was a risk-off, catalyst-light session: VIX rose 14.247%, JPY was the strongest major (+0.211%) and EUR the weakest (-0.231%). BOJ and US ECI both printed inline but still produced brief JPY/USD strength, while German GDP beat did little for EUR. Most legs had no clear catalyst, with EUR/USD closing -17.6 pips and DXY nearly flat (+0.01%).

themes.evidence: VIX rose 14.247%, JPY +0.211% strongest, CHF +0.145%, EUR -0.231% weakest.
German Prelim GDP q/q printed 0.2% vs 0.1% forecast but EUR was weakest major; EUR/USD -17.6 pips with base share 0.76 from EUR.
BOJ and US ECI inline, German GDP and Canada GDP muted; most legs had no clear catalyst.

currency_drivers.USD: Inline ECI produced brief USD strength but overall index still lower on safe-haven flows.
currency_drivers.EUR: German GDP beat at 0.2% but basket response muted; euro was weakest major.
currency_drivers.JPY: Inline BOJ and muted press conference; yen still strengthened, likely safe-haven flow.
currency_drivers.GBP: No own releases; attempted rally was rejected, closing only modestly higher.
currency_drivers.AUD: No own releases; commodity currency weakened, then rejected selling.
currency_drivers.CAD: GDP missed at 0.0% vs 0.2% but reaction was muted, closing at session best.
currency_drivers.CHF: No own releases; safe-haven bid drove strength before giving back 75%.
currency_drivers.NZD: No own releases; sold to -0.20% then recovered, ending nearly flat.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD had an early +38.0 pip rise, then a BOJ-press-aided -28.6 pip drop, a Spain-data +23.5 pip bounce, a Canada-GDP-driven -61.0 pip drop, a late +27.9 pip no-news bounce, and a -18.7 pip fade, netting -17.6 pips.

polarity_reads.read: Inline decision but JPY still strengthened 0.068%, suggesting positioning was flat and safe-haven demand drove yen.
Inline at 0.8% but USD strengthened 0.118%, indicating market leaned long USD or read wage inflation as hawkish.
Beat at 0.2% vs 0.1% but EUR basket moved only 0.008%, showing euro upside lacked conviction.
Canada GDP 0.0% vs 0.2% but basket moved -0.010% inside noise, so no clear CAD positioning read.
Muted 0.028% basket move; no material positioning signal.

scenarios.name: Risk-off continuation
scenarios.thesis: VIX surged 14.247% with JPY leading at +0.211% and CHF at +0.145%; if sentiment remains risk-averse, safe havens extend.
triggers: ISM Manufacturing PMI comes in below 54.7

pair_paths.rationale: EUR weakest at -0.231%; risk-off with USD mixed pushes pair lower.
JPY strongest at +0.211%; safe-haven demand is direct JPY bid.
CHF +0.145% on safe-haven flows, USD flat-to-weaker.

scenarios.name: US data and positioning rebound
scenarios.thesis: Inline ECI still produced USD strength of 0.118%; a strong ISM Manufacturing PMI above 54.7 can trigger a USD short squeeze.

pair_paths.rationale: USD rebound after brief ECI strength; EUR leg down -61.0 pips shows path when USD firms.
GBP rally rejected; USD strength pressures cable toward prior down leg of -51.4 pips.
Previous USD/JPY recovery leg was +47.4 pips; if USD bounces, similar magnitude possible.

scenarios.name: Choppy range, no catalyst
scenarios.thesis: Most legs had no clear catalyst and event reactions were muted; prices likely stay range-bound.
scenarios.invalidation: Sustained break of EUR/USD 78.1 pips range

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD traded a 78.1 pip range on the day; no clear driver to extend.
GBP/USD range was 73.2 pips; mixed GBP vs USD drivers keep it contained.
USD/JPY traded a 101.8 pip range; lack of fresh catalyst argues for range.
